newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes easier, wary of Bundesbank.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes easier, wary of Bundesbank.

text.p: Gold prices were lower and the market uncertain on Thursday morning following overnight news that the Bundesbank might revalue its vast bullion reserves.

Dealers said a weaker dollar had encouraged buying of gold, taking some of the selling pressure off the metal after reports in German newspapers that a junior party in the Bonn coalition government was pushing for gold sales rather than higher taxes to relieve the government deficit.
"Forget the small print, it's being talked about," said one senior dealer of the comments on the Bundesbank, hitherto seen as a major supporter of holding gold as an asset.
The Bundesbank holds its regular council meeting today at which Finance Minister Theo Waigel plans to discuss revaluing the gold reserves, according to a ministry spokeswoman.

Despite the concerns over sales or revaluation of Germany's 95 million ounces of gold reserves, bullion was fixed just $1.00 lower at $347.10 per ounce, recovering slightly from lower prices in New York where the Bundesbank story broke.
"The dollar was weaker against the yen overnight which encouraged some buying in the Far East," a dealer said, adding that "it had done well" to resist pressure to take it lower.
"The German stories are not new. Junior partners in the government there have been advocating selling gold to avoid raising taxes for a long time," he added.
The dealer added that revaluing gold reserves would make sense, however. Germany's gold is valued at around 144 marks per ounce versus a current market price of about 600 marks.
A revaluation closer to the market price would increase the value of German gold reserves by over 40 billion marks.

"A revaluation closer to market values means the bank would have to be a lot more alert (to prices changes) so we could see the Bundesbank offer swaps and options in the years to come," a dealer said.

Meanwhile if buying support at $347.50 continued, a move up powered by the weaker dollar to re-test $350.00 resistance was possible today. "It's still range-bound but we will probably look at the top rather than the bottom end," a dealer said.
Platinum and palladium were also supporting gold and platinum fixed at its highest level since February 28.

"The Russians may have said they will start exporting again soon but people need the metal now which is why the price is still so high," a dealer said. Platinum was barely changed at $394.50/$395.50 and palladium was down $2.00 at $173.00/$174.00. Silver was off two cents at $4.83/$4.85.
